name: BrowserSkill
description: Let AI agents use your real, logged-in browser without interrupting your work. CLI + extension for browser automation across any shell-capable AI agent.
one_liner: Lets an AI assistant borrow your already-logged-in web browser to do tasks for you, filling forms, checking sites, clicking through workflows, without you having to hand over passwords or build a bot.
buyer: A small e-commerce operator who needs recurring manual browser tasks (price checks, marketplace inventory updates, form submissions) done without hiring a virtual assistant.
business_use_cases: An e-commerce seller has an agent log into supplier and marketplace dashboards nightly to reconcile inventory, using their real logged-in session.
A local real-estate agent has an agent check and re-list properties on portals that don't offer an API.
A small agency offers 'browser task automation' as a service for clients whose tools have no API, billing per automated workflow.

money_ideas.idea: Build and sell pre-made automation recipes for common no-API business tasks (marketplace relisting, portal form-filling)
Offer a managed automation service where you build and maintain browser workflows for non-technical clients

steal_this: This weekend, build one automation recipe for a task real small businesses do by hand (e.g. reposting a listing across three marketplaces) and sell it as a done-for-you service.
